answer: By convention, share your repository page to GitHub (or any other repo) as `REPO.md`. Each pointer needs two keys: `name` and `uri`. The optional keys are `description`, `author` and `website`. Pointers are data objects tagged `#meta/library/remote` on a page tagged `#meta/repository`, for example `Repository/myuser`.

7	Repositories are a collection of _pointers_ to [[Library|Libraries]] to install. Their purpose is to offer a curated list of libraries to install.
8	
9	By default, SilverBullet ships with two repositories: [[^Repositories/Std]] with a curated selection of community libraries, and [[^Repositories/SilverBulletMD]] with optional libraries maintained by the SilverBullet project. More can be installed via the [[Workbench/Libraries|Library Manager]].
10	
11	The built-in repositories update like any other: the first update stores a copy in your space, which from then on takes the place of the shipped version. Deleting that copy brings the shipped version back, so built-in repositories can’t be removed.
12	
13	Repositories are implemented on top of a few SilverBullet mechanisms, specifically they are simply [[Meta Page|Meta Pages]] tagged with `#meta/repository` that contain [[Tag/data|data objects]] tagged with `#meta/library/remote` with a `name` and `uri` attribute. Libraries are kept up to date using the [[Share]] mechanism.

15:* **Check for updates**: compares each installed library and repository with its source, and shows the result beside it (see below).
21:* **Available**: the libraries your repositories offer, grouped by repository, with the recommended Std repository first. **Install** puts one in your space. Available library titles open their configured website. When no website is configured, the title opens the library’s source page using the browser URL for its URI (for example, expanding a `github:` URI to its GitHub file page).
22:* **Repositories**: the [[Repository|repositories]] you added, with **Update all** to refresh all of them. Any that fail are listed with the reason. The built-in repositories (Std and SilverBulletMD) update like the others but can’t be removed.

61	You’ll notice that a few [[Share]] related frontmatter keys were set in your local copy. You can now make further changes to your library and run the `Share: Page` command again. After entering another commit message your page will be pushed again. This is how you publish new versions of your library for other people to use.
62	
63	If you used `files` to include additional assets, you have to commit those to the repository through other means.
64	
65	Your library is now ready to install, you can test this by running `Library: Install` in a fresh space. As URI use the value of what is generated under `share.uri` in your library’s frontmatter.
66	
67	You can now [broadcast that your library is ready to install](https://community.silverbullet.md/c/plugs-libraries/14)!
68	
69	# Create a repository
70	If you develop a few libraries, it may be good to make them more discoverable. To do so, you can group them in a [[Repository|Repository]].
71	
72	For this, create another page in your space, this time under `Repository/`, e.g. `Repository/myuser` and tag it with `#meta/repository`.
73	
74	In the page body, put a list of all your libraries, encoded as [[Tag/data|data objects]] as follows:
75	
76	    ---
77	    tags: meta/repository
78	    ---
79	    This is my curated list of awesome libraries!
80	
81	    ```#meta/library/remote
82	    name: Library1
83	    description: This is my first awesome library
84	    website: http://url.com/to/docs
85	    uri: https://github.com/myuser/silverbullet-libraries/blob/main/Library1.md
86	    ---
87	    name: Library2
88	    description: This is my second awesome library
89	    uri: https://github.com/myuser/silverbullet-libraries/blob/main/Library2.md
90	    ```
91	
92	Required keys are:
93	* `name`: a descriptive name of your library.
94	  **Note**: this name is _not_ used as an installation location, the installation location is determined by the `name` key in the library itself.
95	* `uri`: The URI to install the library from.
96	
97	Additional recommended keys are:
98	* `description`: a more elaborate description of the library and its functionality
99	* `author`: who developed this library
100	* `website`: a website URL for more information
101	
102	Now share this repo page using [[Share]] to the same github repo (or any other, it doesn’t really matter), and call it `REPO.md` (by convention).
103	
104	Then announce to the [community](https://community.silverbullet.md/c/plugs-libraries/14) that your repo is open for business and they can add it via the `Library: Add Repository` command (using the same `share.uri` set in your frontmatter).
